AcceptedInvitationOut.description:
After accepting an invitation: the signed-in account and the workspace it joined.
(Here, not in workspaces.schemas, which this module imports.)
AcceptedInvitationOut.title: AcceptedInvitationOut

ConfirmIn.description: What the user confirmed in the review. Nothing becomes a task without it.
ConfirmIn.title: ConfirmIn

DocumentSearchIn.description: A search in the letters of the workspace. POST, so the term is never in a URL.
DocumentSearchIn.title: DocumentSearchIn

DuplicateOut.description:
Two letters that are probably one letter scanned twice. `first` and `second` are in
id order; the caller sees both.
DuplicateOut.title: DuplicateOut

EmptyTrashIn.description:
Empty the trash up to the newest `trashed_at` the caller showed (all when absent):
a letter trashed while the admin read the question is not emptied. With an offset
only (422 otherwise): a moment without one would be read in the server's zone.
EmptyTrashIn.title: EmptyTrashIn

InvitationInfoOut.description: What the invitee sees before accepting; nothing else about the workspace.
InvitationInfoOut.title: InvitationInfoOut

InvitationOut.description: An open invitation, for admins. The token is never read back.
InvitationOut.title: InvitationOut

MyExportOut.description: The member's own export of their post.
MyExportOut.title: MyExportOut

PageMetaIn.description: One page of an upload, in page order.
PageMetaIn.title: PageMetaIn

SessionOut.description: A web session of the caller ("Waar je bent ingelogd").
SessionOut.title: SessionOut

SnippetPartOut.description: A piece of the fragment; `hit` pieces are what matched. Plain text, never HTML.
SnippetPartOut.title: SnippetPartOut

TaskTwinOut.description:
A done task on one letter with an equal open task on the other: a merge that keeps
`open_document_id` can complete it (`complete_twin_tasks`).
TaskTwinOut.title: TaskTwinOut

TrashListOut.description: The caller's trash, the most recently trashed first (at most 500).
TrashListOut.title: TrashListOut

TrashedDocumentOut.description:
A letter in the trash: its summary row, when and by whom it was trashed, and when
it is purged (clients never compute the retention themselves).
TrashedDocumentOut.title: TrashedDocumentOut

UploadMetadataIn.description: The `metadata` field of `createDocument`, as a JSON string.
UploadMetadataIn.title: UploadMetadataIn

post.description: 429 too_many_attempts with Retry-After: five wrong passwords for this email from this address, thirty from this address, or, from a browser that never signed in to this account, more than ten for the account from anywhere (then a wait that doubles from 15 seconds to at most 15 minutes).
Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated.

Set a new password with the token from a reset link's fragment and sign in; every other session of the account ends. 400 reset_link_invalid for an unknown, used, expired or revoked link, or when its maker may no longer act on the account; 422 when the password rules refuse it (the link stays usable). Every paired device and every other open reset link of the account is revoked.

Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Type the password again before an action that needs a recent sign-in (creating a pairing code answers 403 reauthentication_required otherwise). 400 wrong_password; wrong passwords count for the same lockout as signing in (429).

Pair from a brievie://server link without sending the code: proof = HMAC-SHA256(PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(code, 'brievie-pair-v1' + pairing_id, 600000), 'brievie-pair-v1' + nonce + trust binding), the binding being the pinned CA's SHA-256 or the host name connected to. 400 pairing_challenge_invalid for an unknown, expired or used nonce; 400 pairing_code_invalid for a wrong proof or a code that cannot pair (five wrong proofs burn the code).
A one-time nonce (five minutes) for pairDeviceWithProof. Takes no input and reveals nothing about any pairing code.

Web session only. A bearer token (even a valid one) is not accepted here and answers 401 not_authenticated; a session without a valid CSRF token answers 403. A session that signed in more than 15 minutes ago answers 403 reauthentication_required: call reauthenticate first. The response carries the code once and is not stored (Cache-Control: no-store). server_link opens the app without the code: it pairs with a proof.

Join with the invitation's role and sign in. account `new`: name, email address and password (the rules of every account; 409 account_exists when the address has an account, which says that it has one, as registering does). account `existing`: the account's email address and password, with the sign-in lockout (401 invalid_credentials, 429 too_many_attempts); a deactivated account is reactivated. 403 invitation_email_mismatch when the invitation is for another address; 409 already_member, invitation_person_taken; 422 for another account kind. 400 invitation_invalid for an unknown, used, expired or revoked link, or one whose maker is no admin of the workspace any more (one sentence for all).

What an invitation link offers, before accepting: the workspace's name, who invited, the role, whether only one email address can accept, the person and the workspace's AI line. The token from the link's fragment goes in the body. 400 invitation_invalid for an unknown, used, expired or revoked link, or one whose maker is no admin of the workspace any more (one sentence for all).

put.description: Choose the language of the interface and of the server's messages for the caller's account (`nl`, `en`, or `` to follow Accept-Language again). The choice wins over Accept-Language on every later request.

get.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Notices not dismissed yet, oldest first.

post.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Ids of other users' notices, unknown ids and notices this session may not dismiss are left as they are.
Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. 400 wrong_password when the current password is wrong; every other session ends.

get.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated.

delete.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Ending the current session signs this browser out.

get.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The server's log (accounts, sessions, devices), for server admins only (else 403 forbidden). Filters: `user_id` (rows where the user acted or was acted on), `code` (one of the log's codes, else 422), `since` and `until` (whole days in Amsterdam time, both inclusive), `before` (rows strictly older than this moment: pass the last row's `created_at` for the next page). Newest first.

Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The server's log as a CSV download, for server admins only. Filters: `user_id` (rows where the user acted or was acted on), `code` (one of the log's codes, else 422), `since` and `until` (whole days in Amsterdam time, both inclusive), `before` (rows strictly older than this moment: pass the last row's `created_at` for the next page). Newest first. Up to 10,000 rows with the same filters (`limit` does not apply); when more match, the newest are given, the header `X-Brievie-Truncated: true` is set and the last line says so. A cell that would start a spreadsheet formula gets a leading apostrophe.

Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The account's active devices. A server admin may do this for anyone else; a workspace admin only for a member whose only workspace is theirs and who is no server admin (403 server_admin_only). 403 own_account for the caller's own account; 404 user_not_found for an unknown account or one outside the caller's workspaces.

delete.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Revokes the device; the member gets a notice. 404 device_not_found when the account has no such active device. A server admin may do this for anyone else; a workspace admin only for a member whose only workspace is theirs and who is no server admin (403 server_admin_only). 403 own_account for the caller's own account; 404 user_not_found for an unknown account or one outside the caller's workspaces.

post.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. A one-time link (24 hours) with which the member chooses a new password; the token is in its fragment and is shown only here. An earlier unused link stops working. A server admin may do this for anyone; a workspace admin only for a member whose only workspace is theirs and who is no server admin (403 server_admin_only). 403 own_account for the caller's own account; 404 user_not_found for an unknown account or one outside the caller's workspaces; 409 account_inactive; 429 after 30 links in 10 minutes by the same caller.

delete.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Ends every web session of the account; the member gets a notice. A server admin may do this for anyone else; a workspace admin only for a member whose only workspace is theirs and who is no server admin (403 server_admin_only). 403 own_account for the caller's own account; 404 user_not_found for an unknown account or one outside the caller's workspaces.

get.description: How the workspace's letters are read: `off`, `external` or `local`. For `external` also the supplier, the host the text goes to and since when (the moment of consent). An administrator also gets the model. No full address and no key.

put.description: Set how the workspace's letters are read. Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Administrators only. Switching to an external address without consent in force answers 409 `ai_consent_required` unless `consent_address` is exactly the address these settings lead to: first show the notice of `previewAiSettings`. Without `api_key` the stored key stays, at the same address only. The key is never returned.

get.description: The AI autopilot of the workspace: whether letters are put under persons and labels (`auto_organise`) and confirmed (`auto_confirm`) without anybody checking first, whether the server `allowed` it, and the `notice` to agree to. Any member.

put.description: Switch the AI autopilot on or off. Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Administrators only. A switch that goes on needs `acknowledged` (409 `ai_autopilot_ack_required`), AI on for the workspace (409 `ai_autopilot_needs_ai`) and the server's permission (409 `ai_autopilot_forbidden`). Switching off always works. Switching AI off or agreeing to another AI address also switches both off. `acknowledged` with a switch on records that the current `notice` was agreed to (clears `notice_outdated`), also when no switch changes.

post.description: Check AI settings without saving them. Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. When saving them needs consent, `notice` is the text to show (the same `configure_ai` prints) and `address` is what to send back as `consent_address`. Administrators only.

get.description: The external AI services with a preset, and the country each one is in.

Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The workspace's log, for its admins only (another role answers 403 forbidden). At most `limit` rows (1 to 500, default 100). Filters: `user_id` (rows where the user acted or was acted on), `code` (one of the log's codes, else 422), `since` and `until` (whole days in Amsterdam time, both inclusive), `before` (rows strictly older than this moment: pass the last row's `created_at` for the next page). Newest first.

Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The workspace's log as a CSV download, for its admins only. Filters: `user_id` (rows where the user acted or was acted on), `code` (one of the log's codes, else 422), `since` and `until` (whole days in Amsterdam time, both inclusive), `before` (rows strictly older than this moment: pass the last row's `created_at` for the next page). Newest first. Up to 10,000 rows with the same filters (`limit` does not apply); when more match, the newest are given, the header `X-Brievie-Truncated: true` is set and the last line says so. A cell that would start a spreadsheet formula gets a leading apostrophe.

The newest 200 documents. `inbox_state` (`new`, `review` or `unassigned`), `person_id`, `label_id` and `automatic` narrow the list; together they all apply. `automatic=true` keeps the documents the AI confirmed itself or put a label or addressee on (see `confirmed_by_ai`, `auto_label_ids`, `auto_addressee_ids`).

post.description: Upload a scanned document as multipart/form-data: `metadata` is a JSON string (schema `UploadMetadataIn`), followed by one `page` file (image/jpeg) per page in page order. Repeating an upload with the same `client_id` and pages answers 200 with the existing document. 429 `too_many_uploads` with Retry-After when the member or the workspace uploaded too much in a short time (by default 60 per member per 10 minutes, 600 per workspace per hour).

Search the letters of the workspace by their text, sender, summary, label names and person names; every word must match, as a word beginning (Dutch stems too). Best first, then newest. The filters narrow the search; together they all apply. When nothing matches exactly, letters with similar words are answered with `fuzzy=true`. A BSN in `q` is removed before searching (`bsn_removed`). `next_offset` is null on the last page (offset at most 1000). Each hit has a fragment (`snippet`) with the matched words marked. The term is never logged. 422 `validation_error` for a term over 200 characters, an unknown `inbox_state` or `document_type`, or `date_from` after `date_to`; 429 after 30 searches a minute.

Store the review; the document becomes done. When the confirm hands the letter to someone else (the caller no longer sees it), the answer has `can_read` false and holds the id and status only. A repeat of the same review answers the same.

Reverse a label or addressee a rule or the autopilot added (`can_undo`; origin `rule`, `ai` or `name_match`); it is not made again on this document. 409 `event_not_undoable` when the change is not one of those, was undone already or is gone anyway.

Takes back the AI's confirmation: the document returns to review, the confirmed fields are emptied and the tasks the AI made that are still open are removed. 409 document_not_reopenable unless the AI confirmed the document.

Put a letter back from the trash, as it was (role member or admin). A letter that is not in the trash answers unchanged. 404 `document_not_found` once its purge started, or for a letter the caller does not see. Written to the log (`document_restored`).
Make the proposed change. Accepting an accepted proposal changes nothing.
Say no to a proposal; the document does not change and nothing automatic proposes or makes this change on it again.

Move the letter to the trash (role member or admin; a viewer gets 403). It is gone from every list, count, search and task list, and can be put back with `restoreDocument` until `purge_after` (30 days); then it is purged for good. Trashing a letter in the trash again answers the same. 404 `document_not_found` for a letter the caller does not see. Written to the log (`document_trashed`).

get.description: The open pairs of letters that are probably one letter scanned twice, newest first (at most 100). A viewer gets an empty list. Only a pair whose two letters the caller both sees; any other answers as a missing one (404 `duplicate_not_found`).

One open pair with what is the same and what differs. 404 `duplicate_not_found` for a decided pair and for a viewer. Only a pair whose two letters the caller both sees; any other answers as a missing one (404 `duplicate_not_found`).

post.description: The two letters are two letters (role member or admin; a viewer gets 403): the pair is never proposed again. 409 `duplicate_not_open` when already decided. Only a pair whose two letters the caller both sees; any other answers as a missing one (404 `duplicate_not_found`).

The two letters are one (role member or admin; a viewer gets 403). The kept letter gets the other's labels, addressees and open tasks; with `complete_twin_tasks` a task done on the other letter completes its open equal on the kept one (`task_twins`). The other letter goes to the trash (`restoreDocument` takes it back for 30 days; the merge itself is not undone). Answers the kept letter. 409 `duplicate_not_open` when already decided, `duplicate_visibility_differs` when the letters are not seen by the same people (`can_merge`), `document_processing`, `document_retained`; 422 `validation_error` for a `keep_document_id` outside the pair. Written to the log (`document_trashed`, reason `duplicate`). Only a pair whose two letters the caller both sees; any other answers as a missing one (404 `duplicate_not_found`).

get.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. For the workspace's admins: another role answers 403 forbidden, a workspace the caller is not a member of 404 workspace_not_found. Invitations neither used nor revoked, newest first; status open or expired.

post.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. For the workspace's admins: another role answers 403 forbidden, a workspace the caller is not a member of 404 workspace_not_found. A one-time link to join with the given role; the token is in its fragment and is shown only here (Cache-Control: no-store). 404 person_not_found; 409 person_already_linked, already_member (the email address is a member's); 422 email_required.

delete.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. For the workspace's admins: another role answers 403 forbidden, a workspace the caller is not a member of 404 workspace_not_found. The link stops working. 404 invitation_not_found for a used, revoked or unknown one.

post.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. For the workspace's admins: another role answers 403 forbidden, a workspace the caller is not a member of 404 workspace_not_found. A new link with the same role, person, email address, note and validity; the old link stops. Shown only here (Cache-Control: no-store). 404 invitation_not_found; 409 and 422 as when making one.
Create the start set's labels that are missing (matched on `system_key`, then on name); existing labels stay as they are. Returns all labels.

delete.description: Also removes the label from its documents (their history keeps its name) and its preset rule. 409 `label_in_use` when another rule names the label.

post.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The caller leaves the workspace (any role). With their last membership their account is switched off and this session has ended when the answer comes. 404 workspace_not_found; 409 last_admin for the only admin of the workspace, or the last server admin.

delete.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. For the workspace's admins: another role answers 403 forbidden, a workspace the caller is not a member of 404 workspace_not_found. The member leaves the workspace; their person stays without the account link and their tasks here lose their assignee. With their last membership the account is switched off: its sessions end and its devices stop. 403 server_admin_only when that would switch off a server admin and the caller is none; 404 member_not_found; 409 last_admin for the only admin of the workspace, or the last server admin.

put.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. For the workspace's admins: another role answers 403 forbidden, a workspace the caller is not a member of 404 workspace_not_found. Give a member another role; the member sees it at their next request. 404 member_not_found for somebody who is no member of this workspace; 409 last_admin for demoting the only admin. A demoted admin's open invitations and reset links stop.

get.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The caller's own export: `none`, `pending`, `ready` or `failed`, and whether the workspace allows exporting. Never another member's.

post.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Any member asks for an export of their own post: the letters on their name, as a ZIP of the page images and their data. A job builds it; poll `getMyExport`. The file can be downloaded for 24 hours, by the member who asked for it only. A newer request replaces an older export. 403 `export_not_allowed` when an admin switched exports off in this workspace, 409 `export_running` while the last one is being built, 429 after five requests in an hour. Written to the log (`export_created`).

get.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The caller's own finished export as a download (`Cache-Control: private, no-store`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`). 404 `export_not_found` for none, an expired or unfinished one, and for anybody else's: an admin cannot download a member's export. 403 `export_not_allowed` when exports were switched off since. Written to the log (`export_downloaded`).

200.description: The export as a ZIP file, streamed

delete.description: Admins only (403 `forbidden` for others): `person_in_use` also counts letters the caller cannot see, so only an admin learns that a person is in use.

put.description: `name_variants` and `archived` left out keep the person's current value (a rename never archives, restores or clears the variants); sent, they replace it.
Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Link the person to a member of the workspace (`user_id`), or unlink it (null). Administrators only.

get.description: The workspace's rules in the order they run.

post.description: Appended after the other rules; at most 200 per workspace.

put.description: Every rule of the workspace exactly once, in the new order; else 422.

get.description: Example rules to start from, with blanks: a condition with an empty `value` is typed by the user, and the label or person of every action is picked by the user. The same list for every workspace; `kinds` says whom each is meant for.

post.description: Checks the unsaved rule against the newest 500 documents that are not being processed and counts those whose conditions hold. Stores nothing. Reads at most the first 100,000 characters of each document and 2,000,000 in all, so it can stop earlier; `checked_count` says how many documents it checked.

delete.description: History events keep the rule's name.

post.description: Queues applying the rule to the existing documents in the background. 409 `rule_inactive` when the rule is switched off.

get.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. The workspace's settings, for every member.

put.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. For the workspace's admins: another role answers 403 forbidden, a workspace the caller is not a member of 404 workspace_not_found. Change settings; a setting left out stays as it is. A change is written to the log.

get.description: `status` is `open` (default), `done` or `all`. By deadline, undated last; at most 500. 422 `validation_error` for another status.

post.description: Idempotent. Writes a `task_completed` event on the task's document.
Idempotent. Writes a `task_reopened` event on the task's document.

get.description: The letters in the trash the caller sees, the most recently trashed first (at most 500), with when and by whom, and `purge_after`; `total` counts them all.

post.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Purge every letter in the caller's trash for good (role admin), up to `up_to`: the newest `trashed_at` the caller showed (all when absent). Letters the caller does not see stay. Answers how many letters are now being purged; a job removes them. Written to the log, one `document_purged` row per letter.

delete.description: Web session only: a bearer token answers 401 not_authenticated. Purge a letter from the trash now, for good (role admin). Only a letter in the caller's trash: a live letter, one whose purge started, or one the caller does not see answers 404 `document_not_found`. From this answer on it cannot be restored; a job removes its scanned pages and its rows. A back-up made earlier still holds it. Written to the log (`document_purged`).
